might just be me, but if you go on the NHS app to “Book a GP appointment” (because we all know how calling at 8am usually goes), follow the prompts, and then receive a confirmation complete with a calendar invite titled “GP Appointment”…

…I’d say 99% of people would reasonably assume they’d actually secured a GP appointment.

So imagine my surprise when I turned up for said “appointment” only to be told, in the most empathetic and understanding manner imaginable (not), that it wasn’t an appointment at all.

Despite being booked via a section literally titled “Book Appointment”.Despite receiving a “Your GP Appointment” invitation.Despite being given a time slot.

No, no – this was simply to inform me that someone would be “looking at my request”. Not seeing me. Not calling me. Just… looking.

And apparently, it’s always been that have attended Westway for 2.5 years now. The Surgery has become busier with patients facing an onward battle of getting an appointment the same day.
We are made to que or ring up at 8m each day to then have to wait in another que to see if we were quickier then someone else in order to get to see a GP.
You are not elected a Doctor to you so in many cases you need to recall information once again as your notes are not looked at as you only have 10 mins per visit.
I have also experienced a lack of empathy at times by receptionists who have felt it ok to read out loud a run down of all my Medical issues for others to hear.  I'm sure this is against the Confidelity clause they would have signed up for. This has made my time here very stressful and annoying.
I understand the surgery has become busier and god forbid going forward with all the new housing going up how this surgery would be able to look after it's parishioners moving ahead.
The Doctors as far as I know do a fantastic job seeing to us but the 10 min appointments creates a sterile and stressful time for it's patients. Sick people should not be made to fight for more time or appointments,the surgery needs to expand itself with more Doctors and easier booking times. Maghull has grown in numbers over this time yet we are still in a village
